newsitem.title: UK: UK PMI services index to help balance data scales. [CORRECTED 14:30 GMT]
newsitem.headline: UK PMI services index to help balance data scales. [CORRECTED 14:30 GMT]

text.p: The Chartered Institute of Purchasing and Supply will publish its first purchasing managers index for Britain's services sector on Thursday (corrects from Wednesday), April 3.
The survey will cover all sectors, apart from retail and wholesale, tracking levels of business activity, new and outstanding business, average prices changes, operating costs and employment.
Reuters will exclusively release the survey at 0930 GMT which is generally available from 1000 GMT.
The new survey should help plug a hole in the British economic data set which is heavily skewed in favour of manufacturing, despite its dwindling role in the economy.
"Any more information on the services sector will be very welcome indeed. The authorities have clearly recognised the need for it," said Philip Shaw, chief economist at Union Plc.

The recovery in the manufacturing economy has lagged badly the lively pick up in activity in services and retail. Some economists believe that if there were more reliable information available on services, monetary policy would be tighter.

Despite manufacturing comprising just over a quarter of the economy, there is a wealth of official data and survey evidence on the sector including official monthly figures and a batch of private sector surveys.

In stark contrast, the much bigger services sector is measured only once a quarter by the Office for National Statistics (ONS) and in one quarterly business inquiry, courtesy of the British Chambers of Commerce.
The CIPS already produces a monthly purchasing managers index on manufacturing. Economists say it has enjoyed a good track record in forecasting manufucturers' fortunes.
Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke has been accused by some independent analysts of concentrating too much on the manufacturing sector when setting monetary policy.
"But it's not surprising...he is bombarded with data showing continued weakness in that sector," said David Philpotts, UK economist at Schroders.

Manufacturing output increased by just 1.6 percent in the year to February but with consumer spending forecast to grow at four percent or faster this year, there is clearly plenty of money around and Britain's booming service sector appears to be the prime beneficiary.

In its last inflation report, the Bank of England, which has long bemoaned the lack of concrete statistics on services, said that while the strong pound has subdued the manufacturing sector, the service and retail sectors show more signs of inflationary pressure.
Clarke has been at loggerheads with the Bank's governor, Eddie George, who for months has been demanding an increase in base rates from six percent.

The ONS has made significant advances in the information it provides on the services sector, but it comes out only once a quarter with the most useful information released up to three months after the end of the period.
Plans at the ONS for monthly releases of the services sector have been shelved due to funding contraints.
But analysts said it is questionable how useful monthly releases on services would be.

"I think there is a case for saying the source of information on services is not reliable enough. The data are usually revised quite a lot and you have to question how much use they would be as a first release," said Shaw.
